findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign the deleted-env-vars and bridge_state/-move portions of criterion 8 to a specific story (e.g. S5 records the env-var deletions and S8 records the bridge_state move in CHANGELOG/release notes).
evidence: Criterion 8: 'Release notes and CHANGELOG record the package rename, the deleted env vars, and the bridge_state/ move.'
S1 bullet: 'criteria 1 and 2 for src/, part of criterion 8' — only 'part'
S5 lists 'criteria 5 and 6 part'; S8 lists 'criterion 7' — neither claims criterion 8
findings.finding: Criterion 8 (release notes + CHANGELOG record the package rename, the deleted env vars, and the bridge_state/ move) is only partially covered by the child decomposition: S1 claims 'part of criterion 8' (the package rename), but no story is assigned the deleted-env-vars portion (produced by S5) or the bridge_state/ move portion (produced by S8). The env-var and retention portions of criterion 8 have no covering story.
scenarios: S5 deletes three env vars but no story owns writing them into CHANGELOG/release notes
S8 moves bridge_state to .rebar/bridge but no story owns documenting the move
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the S5 and S8 decomposition bullets to each claim their slice of criterion 8 (env-var deletions in S5; bridge_state move in S8), with S1 keeping the package-rename slice.

findings.finding: Sibling tickets touch the same file(s) with no ordering edge.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a depends_on/blocks edge to serialize, or partition the file ownership.

evidence: 6 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace 'keep-last-N' with 'keep-last-5' in the Context and S8 bullet so the retention count is named consistently with criterion 7.

scenarios: An executor reading S8 only sees 'keep-last-N' with no value

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State 4b07's true prerequisites: it depends on S3 (f75f) for `rebar.reconciler.guarded_pass._Disposition` and must land after S4's (cfbd) rewrite of tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py, not S1 alone.
evidence: 4b07 Approach step 1: 'replace the sys.path.insert / try / finally block with a plain `from rebar.reconciler.guarded_pass import _Disposition`'

f75f (S3) Scope/Approach: guarded_pass.py is NEW and _Disposition/PassResult/run_pass_result 'move ... out of __main__.py' into it; f75f lists tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py among tests retargeted to guarded_pass
cfbd (S4) Scope lists tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py and rewrites its 3/4/75 translate-at-runner cases via the new engine_stub
Parent 'Child decomposition' line: 'effusive-unsentient-massasauga (found at epic close): drop the last _engine sys.path.insert ... criterion 1 for tests/' — names no S3/S4 ordering
findings.finding: Child 4b07 (effusive-unsentient-massasauga) edits tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py to insert `from rebar.reconciler.guarded_pass import _Disposition`, but the parent's child-decomposition line declares it covering only 'criterion 1 for tests/' and (by its own Context) presupposes only S1 — yet `rebar.reconciler.guarded_pass` is created by S3 (f75f) and the same heldout test is substantially rewritten by S3 (retarget to guarded_pass) and S4 (cfbd, 3/4/75 translate cases + engine_stub). The declared ordering (S1) understates the real prerequisite set (S3 for the module to exist, and layering atop S4's rewrite of the same file).
scenarios: If 4b07 is scheduled/applied before S3 lands, `rebar.reconciler.guarded_pass` does not yet exist and the rewritten import fails
If 4b07 is applied before S4's rewrite of the same test, the two edits collide on the same block/region of test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py
findings.suggested_fix: Record 4b07 as depending on f75f (S3) and cfbd (S4) — or explicitly note it is the epic-close sweep that runs after all stories — so the import target and the shared-file edit ordering are unambiguous.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State S4's timeout-path disposition: say with an explicit disposition word (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent) what the caller surfaces when _bridge_runner times out and reaps the process group.
evidence: AC4 and S4 specify the reap MECHANISM (start_new_session, reap_process_group, no second reaper) and its tests, but carry no disposition word for the timeout outcome
GATE opens: S4 changes how a timeout is handled on the bridge subprocess path
No fallback chain is present, so only clause (1) (per-arm disposition) applies
findings.finding: S4 alters the bridge-subprocess timeout path (direct spawn + process-group reap on timeout) but never states the DISPOSITION the caller surfaces when the subprocess times out and is reaped — is a bridge-sync timeout retryable/transient or fatal/permanent?
findings.location: Child decomposition S4; AC line 4 ('_bridge_runner spawns ... and, on timeout, reaps the process group')
scenarios: The bridge subprocess hangs, _bridge_runner hits the timeout and reaps the group — a caller (CLI/MCP bridge_sync) must know whether to retry or treat the pass as permanently failed
findings.suggested_fix: Add an inline disposition clause to S4/AC4, e.g. 'a subprocess timeout surfaces as a transient/retryable failure (WAIT_AND_RETRY) after the process group is reaped — the reaped pass is not treated as a permanent error.'
